podcasts.name: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Lack of Censorship Concern
podcast.body: Johnny Otis remarked with humor that while his earlier works like "All With Me Henry" and "Willie and the Hand Jive" faced obscenity accusations, the explicit "For Adults Only" album by Snatch and the Poon Tangs, with its "constant sexual insults," surprisingly drew no public concern or bother regarding obscenity. "Otis would in later years laugh that he'd received accusations of obscenity, for all with me Henry and for William the Han Jive, but nobody had seen bothered in the slightest by the records of Snatch and the Poon Tangs with their constant sexual insults."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Preservation of Black Folklore
podcast.body: The album "For Adults Only" by Snatch and the Poon Tangs, despite its explicit content, served Johnny Otis's goal of preserving black folklore. Songs like "The Signifying Monkey," which had been performed for years, were included with their original sexual insults intact, unlike censored versions by other artists like Chuck Berry and Willie Dixon. "Otis wanted to preserve bits of black folklore. Songs like The Signifying Monkey had been performed for years, and had even been recorded by people like Chuck Berry and Willie Dixon, but they'd always stripped out the sexual insults that make up much of the piece's appeal."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
